changes: Phase B is now rendered in the env map's frame of reference. The world mapping stays fixed; all objects, lamps and the camera are children of an empty 'EnvFrame' whose rotation is the mapping rotation M = Rz(-theta)*Rx(-phi). Every frame is the same image as 'locked camera, rotating env', but Cycles now motion-blurs the env rotation: shadows, probe reflection and skylight smear with the same 0.5 shutter as the globe. This fixes the strobing clicks at zero extra cost. Motion steps 3 on every mesh and the camera keep the rigid co-rotation sharp.

Cycles 4.5 bug workaround: with persistent data, a static frame rendered right after a moving frame lost the metal objects and the globe (reproduced: f150/f165/f180 broke when rendered after a moving frame). A 10-micron vertical jitter of the whole rig at half-frames gives every object motion data in every frame. It is invisible: the camera moves with the set, and the loop check still passes.

self_critique:
The day half now reads as a premium toy shot instead of a pale product render. The island fills about 64% of the frame. The probe and globe show a bright candy sky with vivid cards, the shadows are tinted lavender instead of grey, the aqua ring and bigger blue cake add colour blocks, and the ending lands in clear view on the violet tick with the shadow visibly breathing.

Two technical choices did most of the work. Rendering phase B in the env's frame gives physically correct motion blur of the env rotation, which is better than the critic's supersampling (that would have shown 5 discrete shadow copies at 26 deg/f) and costs nothing. Splitting the map into its sun and sky parts let me tint shadows and lift reflections without touching the calibrated sun, the shadow geometry or the loop check. I also found a real Cycles persistent-data bug that round 1 never hit (static frames after moving frames lost every metal object) and guarded against it.

Still weak:
- The snap accents land one frame late (blur onset on the beat, main step on beat+1).
- Saturated pixels are about 9%, not 10%.
- The bunny's flanks go cool lavender/violet but never take on the warm card colours.
- The fast snaps make the shadows briefly faint smears. That is correct and reads as a smear frame, but it could be judged too soft.
- The reversed glide still needs the lead's sign-off.
- I edited the post-tools overlay script, so that owner should review the 8-line change and re-run make_overlays.py.
- Timing numbers are noisy because the GPU was shared.

rejected_critic_items: Strobing clicks, 5-pass sub-frame supersampling (major): replaced by true Cycles motion blur through the EnvFrame rig. It costs nothing (about 0.15 GPU-h saved), and at 26 deg/f five sub-frames would show discrete shadow copies rather than a blur.

Off-beat split, radial POP overshoot of about 8% peaking on f61 (part of a major item): rejected. f61 and f91 would then have different light radii, breaking the closed-form 'f91 = f61 geometry, colours permuted' proof. Instead the lights land on f61 with zero velocity and the halos (which light nothing) pop to 1.2 exactly on f61.

Pale day (d), applying the extra world saturation to the lat-long strip as well: not done, because the strip is a post-tools asset. The saturation goes only to the sky part of the lighting (the sun is left alone so the plate doesn't yellow), and the globe got its own x1.8.
